name: tolerance
description: A calm and deliberate decision to allow something annoying or painful to persist, even when you have some power to make it better.
perceptions: I could do something about it to make myself feel a little better without making the situation worse.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
examples: Putting up with your noisy kids while trying to work at home.

guidance.description: The ability to endure other people or situations that you find annoying, irritating or downright unpleasant—is a crucial part of living and interacting with others.

comparisons.description: 'Acceptance' is what you feel when there's nothing you can do to change the situation. 'Suppressed anger' is when you're afraid that doing or saying something will make the situation worse. 'Tolerance' is used when we could do or say something, but choose not to.

variations.name: social tolerance
variations.description: A deliberate decision to allow someone to persist in a social behavior or characteristic that you find annoying or painful without complaint.
perceptions: Someone has a behavior or characteristic that is annoying or socially wrong.
I could do or say something about it to make myself feel a little better without making the situation worse.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
examples: Not shouting at someone who's politics you disagree with.
Not treating someone negatively because they're a social outsider.

variations.name: high tolerance of discomfort
variations.description: A sense that complaining about minor discomfort is not worthwhile and not part of your identity.
perceptions: I'm in a state of pain or discomfort.
I could do or say something about it to make myself feel a little better.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
examples: Not complaining about an injury so as not to worry others.
Not asking to turn the temperature up when it's chilly to save on utility bills.

commentaries.quote: Tolerance isn't about not having beliefs. It's about how your beliefs lead you to treat people who disagree with you.
Be tolerant with one another and forgive one another whenever any of you has a complaint against someone else.
In the practice of tolerance, one's enemy is the best teacher.
The man who is most aggressive in teaching tolerance is the most intolerant of all: he wants a world full of people too timid and ashamed to really disagree with anything.
What is tolerance? It is the consequence of humanity. We are all formed of frailty and error; let us pardon reciprocally each other's folly - that is the first law of nature.
Chronically insecure people easily lose their altruism, tolerance, and respect for non-conformity.
There are lots of reasons you might tolerate an annoyance. Most of them have to do with your self-identity.
